title: Tesla Inc.
bodyHtml:
Investment Thesis

Tesla is a bet on three simultaneous transitions: EV mass market adoption, Optimus humanoid robot commercialisation, and FSD achieving full autonomy. Each would independently justify a significant valuation. The challenge is that all three have execution risk and require different timelines. The market prices Tesla on EV volumes, which means Optimus and FSD are available at low or zero incremental cost. If either delivers at scale, the re-rating is substantial.

Future Tech Roadmap

Humanoid Robot (Factory Deployment) Confident 2026
Humanoids performing real production tasks commercially: Tesla Giga 2026 target
📈 NVIDIA provides the simulation platform (Isaac Sim) and training infrastructure for every major humanoid robot program. Robot training demand is additive to LLM training demand on the same GPU clusters.
▲ LEADING · 82% vs NVDA 55% · ARM 50%
Grid-Scale Battery Storage (GWh) Confident 2018
Multi-GWh battery installations balancing grids: CATL, Tesla Megapack
📈 Tesla Megapack is the market-leading utility-scale battery product. Order backlog is multi-year. Energy storage is growing faster than Tesla's vehicle business on a percentage basis.
MONOPOLY · 85% no direct rivals identified
SiC Power Semiconductors Confirmed Ongoing
SiC MOSFETs for high-voltage EV powertrains with lower switching losses
📈 Tesla uses SiC MOSFETs extensively in Model 3 and Model Y powertrain inverters. SiC reduces energy loss and enables longer EV range. Tesla is vertically integrating some SiC production.
MONOPOLY · 70% no direct rivals identified
Lithium-Ion Battery Confirmed Ongoing
Rechargeable Li-ion cells powering EVs and grid storage; <$100/kWh
📈 Tesla is one of the largest lithium-ion battery manufacturers globally via the Gigafactory network. Battery cost reduction is the primary driver of EV gross margin improvement.
MONOPOLY · 80% no direct rivals identified
Full Self-Driving Level 4 (Urban) Confident 2028
Urban driving with no human available, approved for general public roads
📈 Tesla FSD is commercially deployed but still Level 2+ (supervised). Level 4 (no human required) is targeted but not committed. Timeline has slipped multiple times. If achieved, transforms the revenue model via autonomous ride-hailing.
⚡ 2ND · 65% behind MBLY 65% (−0pp)
ADAS Level 2 (Partial Automation) Confirmed Ongoing
Combined steering + acceleration automation with driver supervision: Tesla AP
📈 Tesla Autopilot/FSD is deployed across the entire Tesla fleet (7M+ vehicles). This is a paid subscription and a data collection mechanism for training the FSD neural networks.
▲ LEADING · 88% vs MBLY 85%
↑ LEADING · 82% vs NVDA 55% · ARM 50%

Business & Fundamental Analysis

Financial Health & Profitability

Yes, profitable but margins are declining. Tesla generates positive net income and free cash flow. However, its automotive gross margins have compressed from 25%+ to 14-16% due to price cuts in the global EV market.

AI Monetization & Business Goals

Tesla is transitioning from an EV car builder to an autonomous robotics network:

  • FSD (Full Self-Driving): Monetizing unsupervised FSD software subscriptions.
  • Robotaxi: Launching an autonomous ride-hailing network.
  • Optimus Humanoid: Mass-producing humanoid robots for industrial use.

Capital Expenditure (Capex) Concerns

Capex is high, focused on building the Dojo supercomputer and expanding massive GPU clusters (using 100k+ NVIDIA H100s) to train FSD models.

Partnerships & Alliances

  • xAI: Cooperating on compute sharing and AI modeling.
  • Municipalities: Seeking regulatory unlock approvals for driverless robotaxi operation.

Controversies & Headwinds

  • NHTSA Investigations: Ongoing federal safety investigations into Autopilot and FSD accidents.
  • Cybertruck Ramping: High production costs, delays, and multiple recalls.\n
